reply_text:
㊥ ("put together the entire certificate") That changes what I had for R20, and it makes the code side simpler. R20 is the assembly over the other nodes: for each run it says which case of the theory held at each node and whether the recorded numbers agree. It is not a separate gauge to build later.

🈹 (R20 deferred) Last turn I said I would leave R20 until experiments were running, and my table listed it as "not built". Both were based on reading R20 as a separate interoception mechanism. On your reading it is the thing that makes an experiment readable, so it comes first, not last.

㊢ (where it already lives in code) The per-run census I found, `wm/apparatus_certificates.clj`, is this node's implementation site. The full-loop runner calls it on every run and it collects one verdict per node. Today it collects verdicts on the old readings, and it only says present, refused or not applicable. It does not say what happened.

㊭ ("F is the same for every policy or F is not") Each Lean module I have been restating already divides into cases, so the certificate can report the case and then check the numbers against it:

| Node | The cases the certificate would name |
|---|---|
| Precision | F the same for every policy, so temperature unchanged; F favoured the policies G favoured, so more decisive; F went against them, so less decisive |
| Evidence | the observation did not discriminate between states, so belief unchanged; it did, so belief moved |
| Habit | a witnessed success, so that policy's count rose; otherwise unchanged |
| Class preference | before the horizon, risk zero; at the horizon, risk by class, infinite if the predicted class has no preference mass |
| Strategic focus | focus unchanged; focus changed, so the terminal preference changed |
| Liveness | state changed, a live tick; no change, not live |
| Two agents | author and reviewer each took their part; a part was taken twice; a part was dropped |

The overall line is then "every node's record agrees with its case", or it names the node that does not.

㊟ (theory anchor) The literature's short form of "is this active inference" is in Da Costa et al. (2020): agents "perceive the world by minimising variational free energy ... and act by minimising expected free energy", which "can be concisely framed as self-evidencing". Reading R20's interoception as the machine observing whether its own ticks have that form is my mapping. The existing `R20Interoception` module (a preferred range over an internal reading) still fits, with the certificate as the reading and "every node agrees" as the preferred range.

㊭ (order of work)
1. Precision restatement returns from codex-10; I review it.
2. One Lean module for the R20 certificate: the case type per node, the theorem that the cases are exhaustive and each one fixes what the record must show, and the overall predicate. It imports the node modules and adds no new theory.
3. Rewrite the census against it. This is small: it reads records the run already writes, for the nodes where the code already computes the right thing.
4. Habit carrier and R10 follow, each adding a row.

previous_reply_acts.text: ("the war machine has two agents inside of it") Understood, and the split you describe is already how R11 stands. The Lean statement is for any finite set of agents; the code side will be written only for the two the runner casts, the author and the reviewer.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("the theory should generalize if possible") It does, at no extra cost. The R11 record in Lean is a joint step for any finite set of agents: what each believed the shared goal was, the part each played, what each saw of the others, and what each believed afterwards. That fits an episode where claude-4 starts a phase with several agents as well as a War Machine click with two. No theorem in the module depends on the number of agents; only its two worked controls use two.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("one of my instructions might have gotten dropped") That case is already one of the controls I added from the dark-tower reading. The shared-state section asks that every shared item has exactly one writer, and it refuses two cases: both agents taking the item, and neither taking it because each thought it was the other's. A dropped instruction is the second case. The companion theorem says that when the agents agree on who has what, their shares add up to the whole, so nothing is dropped.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
("keep the implementation simple") For the War Machine I will hold R11 to this:
- **Agents:** the author and the reviewer, as named by `FUTON_WM_AUTHOR_AGENT` and `FUTON_WM_REVIEWER_AGENT` in `full_loop_runner.clj`.
- **Evidence:** read from records the run already holds. I will not add a model of other agents to the machine.
- **Check:** the two-agent case of the Lean record. The first question is the one-writer one: did the author write the artefact, did the reviewer write only the verdict, and was every part of the task taken by one of them.
